summary: Validated the new Parcel feature end-to-end on the backend. All 29 unit tests (test_parcels.py + test_jobs_helpers.py) pass, and a new 7-test HTTP-level suite (test_parcels_api.py) hitting the live /api routes also passes. Verified: (1) creating a job with 1 single + 1 parcel(N=3) returns total_stones=4, total_certificates=2 with kind='parcel' & stone_count=3 on the parcel row, (2) is_parcel=true with stone_count<2 is rejected with HTTP 400 mentioning 'stone_count', (3) group-stones rejects a parcel with HTTP 400 'Parcels cannot be added to a certificate group', (4) toggling color_stability_test on a parcel of 3 changes total fee by exactly cs_fee*3 (delta=$150 → cs_fee=$50) and toggling off restores the original, (5) toggling mounted on a parcel of 4 adds the mounted fee ONCE (delta=$50, not $200), (6) POST /api/jobs/{id}/stones with is_parcel/stone_count works and recomputes totals correctly, (7) GET /api/jobs/{id} returns total_certificates. Production-DB parcel canonical pricing confirmed: Sapphire parcel(3) value $15000 Express → base fee $1350 ($450 * 3). Frontend UI walkthrough via Playwright + sessionStorage-injected auth could NOT be completed because the zustand auth-storage shape stored under sessionStorage on this Next.js static export was rejected (all subsequent /api calls returned 401 and the app redirected to /login showing 'Your session expired'). The main agent had already smoke-tested the Kind/Count columns rendering after `yarn build`, so UI rendering itself is presumed working; what could not be independently verified is the end-to-end click flow (Switch toggle → submit → table display 'X stones · Y certs'). Recommend the main agent perform that UI verification via interactive Turnstile, or that we get a working session-restore recipe for the preview env.
action_items: Main agent: perform an interactive UI smoke (Turnstile + create-parcel-job) to confirm the Kind switch, Count input, amber tint, and 'X stones · Y certs' display in the jobs table. All backend behaviour is already validated.

Optional: document the exact sessionStorage/localStorage key + schema that the deployed Next.js bundle expects so future testing agents can bypass Turnstile (current docs say sessionStorage 'auth-storage' { state:{token,user,isAuthenticated}, version:0 } but the live build rejected this — 401 returned to axios despite a valid JWT from /api/auth/login).
critical_code_review_comments: Backend: `_build_stones_for_create` correctly rejects is_parcel with stone_count<2 (HTTP 400). Good.

Backend: PUT /api/stones/{id}/fees response wraps the stone object as {message, stone, total_fee} — frontend already consumes this shape but it's worth noting for any future test consumer (caught my first-pass test).
Backend: parcel fee path (`calculate_parcel_fee_from_brackets`) uses avg-value bracket lookup × N for base + cs_fee*N + mounted_fee*1 — verified live with production pricing brackets.
Backend: total_certificates is now persisted on Job and surfaced on GET /api/jobs/{id} — confirmed in HTTP test.

Auth: external preview returns 403 to non-browser HTTP clients (CF edge) — automated tests must use either the in-cluster URL (http://localhost:8001) or a real browser context for the frontend public URL.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_parcels_api.py tests/test_parcels.py tests/test_jobs_helpers.py -v` as the regression suite for the parcel feature. The HTTP test pulls client_id+branch_id from an existing job via GET /api/jobs?limit=1 and assumes at least one job already seeded in the DB. For UI/Playwright the session-restore recipe under 'auth-storage' sessionStorage key returned 401 in this deployment — interactive Turnstile login is currently the reliable path. To run the HTTP tests you must blank TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY in /app/backend/.env then restart backend (I restored it after testing).
rca of the issue: No bugs found. The previous iteration's two false-positive failures in my first draft (CS-on showing negative delta, mounted-on showing negative delta) were caused by the test reading `t1.json().get('fee')` whereas the PUT /api/stones/{id}/fees endpoint returns a wrapped envelope {message, stone:{...}, total_fee}. Fixed in /app/backend/tests/test_parcels_api.py to read `total_fee` (or `stone.fee`). The group-stones 422 was likewise a test bug — the StoneGroupUpdate schema requires `group_number` in addition to `stone_ids`; added group_number:1 to the payload and the endpoint correctly returns 400 with the expected 'Parcels cannot be added to a certificate group' message.
